blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

items.t: Hazelmere is a rural community and board sub-area on the southeast side of the City of Surrey — the acreage ground around 16 Avenue and 184 Street running south toward 0 Avenue and the US border, also known locally as Hall's Prairie — and one of nine sub-areas of the Fraser Valley board community "S Surrey White Rock", inside the City's South Surrey community. The Little Campbell River winds through it toward Boundary Bay, and much of its watershed is farmland in the Agricultural Land Reserve.
Where the condo stock concentrates: nowhere.

Community context only (whole S Surrey White Rock community, NOT Hazelmere's prices): Detached median $1,628,000; Condos & Townhomes median $700,000 / $524 per sq ft / 99% sale-to-list / 33 DOM. Per-sub-area medians are not published: UNVERIFIED at sub-area level.
This is effectively a car-only sub-area on the sources checked.

Planning frame to the north: the South Campbell Heights Local Area Plan ground sits immediately north of Hazelmere's southern lands; the City's plan document records that Hall's Prairie was renamed Hazelmere after the rail station named for Henry Thrift's homestead, and that Hazelmere largely maintained its rural, agricultural character over the past century.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Hazelmere Guide

items.t: ALR housing frame (governs any Hazelmere parcel in the ALR): land in the ALR may generally have no more than one residence per parcel; a principal residence may be up to 500 m² total floor area without ALC application; one additional detached residence may be permitted of up to 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less, or up to 186 m² on parcels over 40 ha; a secondary suite is permitted only inside the principal residence and only where local bylaws allow it; local governments may further restrict residences through zoning.

SSMUH caution for this ground: Surrey's SSMUH allowances apply to eligible residential-zoned properties under 4,050 m² inside the Urban Containment Boundary, with exemptions including lands not connected to community water and sewer — most Hazelmere acreage ground is outside that shape, so the standard 3–4 unit framing must not be applied to a Hazelmere lot without a parcel check. Where SSMUH does apply, a secondary suite's habitable floor area may not exceed 40% of the principal dwelling's habitable floor area under Bylaw 12000.

blocks.text: Good to know about Hazelmere Guide

items.t: In the guide page's main FAQ section, two questions appear with NO answer — "What heritage sites are in Hazelmere?" and "Which schools serve Hazelmere?" — with both answers appearing only in a second, separate FAQ block lower on the page. No wrong-email instance is documented on this page either (stated explicitly in the flag block above).

The watershed has no dykes. The guide page states (site copy compiled from the City of Surrey per the page) that the Little Campbell River watershed covers over 60 km² from the Township of Langley through Surrey to Boundary Bay, is mostly rural residential and agricultural with a large part in the ALR, has no dykes, and its floodplain follows the river channel closely.

Heritage here is stated as guide-page site copy. Hazelmere United Church, 1614 184 Street, built 1903 in Carpenter Gothic style; Hazelmere Cemetery, 19184 16 Avenue, established when the Hall's Prairie Cemetery Co. incorporated in 1908; and the Hall's Prairie South Building at 18035 8 Avenue, built about 1927 — all three on the City's heritage site list per the guide page, attributed there to City of Surrey heritage pages.
Recreation is private, not municipal, on the sources read.

The feed mixes two different products. At reading it ran from just-under-an-acre homes on city services through estate acreages to large A-1/ALR holdings and a development-framed land parcel — lifestyle acreages and land-value parcels in one feed, with individual card framings that are listing text, not plan confirmations. Price the parcel, not the feed.
Travel time to any hospital: UNVERIFIED.

items.t: Zoning is under Surrey Zoning Bylaw No. 12000 — Hazelmere is predominantly General Agriculture (A-1) zoning over ALR land.

ALR residence rules (the frame that governs most Hazelmere acreage): a principal residence on ALR land is capped at 500 m²; a secondary suite is permitted only inside the principal residence; and ONE additional residence is permitted up to 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less, or up to 186 m² on parcels over 40 ha (Agricultural Land Commission, residences in the ALR: These rules — not the City suite rules — decide what a coach house or second dwelling on a Hazelmere acreage may be.
Secondary suites in Surrey (non-ALR context) are capped at 40% of the principal dwelling's habitable floor area (City of Surrey, secondary suites

SSMUH CAUTION: Surrey's SSMUH allowances (implemented July 8, 2024 — 3 units on lots under 280 m², 4 units over 280 m², up to 6 on eligible lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent bus stop) apply to eligible lots under 4,050 m² inside the Urban Containment Boundary on community water/sewer (City of Surrey, SSMUH: Most Hazelmere acreage sits outside that shape — larger rural lots, ALR designation, private servicing — so SSMUH generally does NOT unlock units here; a parcel-by-parcel check (containment boundary, ALR status, servicing) is required before assuming any allowance applies, and ALR parcels answer to the ALC rules first.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Hazelmere
What trades here

items.t: Lot fabric: Servicing is parcel-specific and varies inside the sub-area: the page's general guidance is private wells and onsite septic for rural homes, yet one feed listing is described in its own text as on city sewer and water — both positions are carried, and neither is generalised to the sub-area. No typical lot size or lot price is stated as a profile.

Fee-simple lots are the default form: an acreage parcel here is fee-simple unless title says otherwise — no strata corporation, no Form B, no strata fees. The one built strata complex in the sub-area, Hazelmere Village, is a townhouse complex (cross-reference below), not a lot form. A sub-area-wide strata-versus-freehold split is UNVERIFIED.

: a bare-land strata lot IS strata tenure on the lot itself — Form B, strata fees for common property and registered bylaws apply to the lot; it is NOT fee-simple. No bare-land strata plan inside Hazelmere was verified in this research — no such plan is named or counted, and tenure on any specific parcel is a title question.

Zoning character, as the page states it (UNVERIFIED on the bylaw text): A-1 General Agriculture zoning for Hazelmere Valley acreages, with Part 10 (Bylaw 12000) minimum lot areas of 4 hectares inside the ALR and 2 hectares outside it for new A-1 lots, one single-family dwelling which may contain one secondary suite under A-1, and RA Acreage Residential zoning on some nearby land with a 4,050 m² minimum. The RA figure is consistent with the City's SSMUH zone table (RA lots at over 4,050 m²); the A-1 / Part 10 figures themselves were not re-read in Bylaw 12000 in the research — confirm in the current consolidated bylaw before quoting them for a parcel.
Built stock — cross-reference ONLY, never land

Assemblies / development sites / rezoning proposals, documented AS SUCH, never as inventory: none is documented as a named proposal in this sub-area's research. Two framing items are documented AS planning context only: (1) a feed parcel whose listing text frames it as land in a townhouse-designated plan area — a listing framing, not a plan confirmation opened in the research; and (2) the South Campbell Heights Local Area Plan ground immediately north — a City plan area, not a development site and not Hazelmere lot inventory.

ALR vs non-ALR split: UNVERIFIED — no ALC map result for a Hazelmere parcel was opened in the research, and no share is stated. Check every parcel on the ALC maps by PID or civic address before pricing it.
: No phase selling vacant lots is documented in this sub-area. Never mixed with built presales.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Hazelmere

items.t: Hazelmere is one of nine sub-areas of the Fraser Valley board community "S Surrey White Rock" in the SnapStats data, inside the City of Surrey's South Surrey community — one of the City's seven communities. (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report)

Names and history: "Hazelmere" (board, City heritage name and page name) and "Hall's Prairie" (the older local name). The City's South Campbell Heights Local Area Plan document records that Hall's Prairie was renamed Hazelmere after the rail station named for Henry Thrift's homestead, and that Hazelmere largely maintained its rural, agricultural character over the past century. That plan ground — approximately 249 hectares centred around 16 Avenue and 192 Street, immediately south of Campbell Heights Business Park — sits immediately north of Hazelmere's southern lands; the 249-hectare figure is carried from the City's display-boards document via search result and was not located in the full plan text in the research's verification pass, so it is UNVERIFIED on the plan text here.

Schools (Ministry-listed names and addresses only): Xw'epiteng Elementary, 18035 8 Ave (the school physically in Hazelmere); East Kensington Elementary, 2795 184 St; Douglas Elementary, 17325 2 Ave; Earl Marriott Secondary, 15751 16 Ave (level read from its name — the Ministry level field mislabels it).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Hazelmere

items.t: ALR block (the governing frame for any Hazelmere parcel that is in the ALR): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); land in the ALR may generally have no more than one residence per parcel — a principal residence up to 500 m² total floor area without ALC application, a secondary suite only inside the principal residence and only where local bylaws allow it, and at most one additional detached residence of up to 90 m² (parcels ≤40 ha) or 186 m² (parcels >40 ha); local governments may further restrict residences through zoning. Farm class is three-tier — $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha / $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha / $10,000 under 0.8 ha, applications by Oct 31 — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR; whether any specific Hazelmere property carries farm-class taxation is a BC Assessment / parcel question, UNVERIFIED in the research.

Secondary suites / coach houses (urban Surrey frame, for completeness — not assumed to govern A-1 ground): one suite per single family, semi-detached or duplex unit, capped at 40% of the principal unit and never inside a coach house or garden suite; coach/garden suites 35–75 m² (up to 120 m² on RA, R2, R2-O and R3 lots below maximum FAR). On A-1 / ALR parcels the ALR block above and the parcel's zone govern first.

blocks.text: Good to know about Hazelmere

items.t: The highest ratio in the set rests on two sales. A land price case here needs parcel-level comparables, not the ratio and not the $1,628,000 community median.
"Partly in the ALR" is a real parcel condition here, not a hedge.

A serviced lot inside a "well and septic" area is not a contradiction. The feed itself carries a just-under-1-acre property described as on city sewer and water alongside the page's rural well/septic guidance — servicing follows the parcel's street and connections, not the sub-area's reputation.

The old name explains the ground. Hall's Prairie became Hazelmere after Henry Thrift's homestead rail station, and the City's plan document says the district kept its rural, agricultural character for a century — the acreage fabric is the historic fabric, not leftover urban lots.

A townhouse-designation framing in a listing is not a plan document. One feed parcel is framed in its own listing text as land in a townhouse-designated plan area; the research opened no plan confirmation for that parcel, so the designation is UNVERIFIED here and is priced only after a COSMOS / plan check.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Hazelmere than in June?
faq.a: In Hazelmere, listings of houses fell from 9 in June to 7 in September (−22.2%); condos and townhomes was 1 in June and 2 in September, too few (under 3) to call a rise or fall.

faq.q: How big is Hazelmere compared with the rest of South Surrey and White Rock?
faq.a: In September 2026, Hazelmere held 1.2% of the 600 houses listed in South Surrey and White Rock and 0.3% of the 593 condos and townhomes listed in South Surrey and White Rock.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Hazelmere from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 3 houses and 0 condos and townhomes sold in Hazelmere over those 4 months.

faq.q: How do I find out which school serves an address in Hazelmere?
faq.a: School catchments are set by address, so use the school district's catchment locator with the exact address. Catchment lines change, so check before you write an offer.

faq.q: Who can help me buy or sell in Hazelmere?
faq.a: Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, works across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361 or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: Is there an apartment condo building in Hazelmere?

faq.a: Where a parcel is in the ALR, the ALC frame in governs: one principal residence to 500 m², a suite only inside it where local bylaws allow, and at most one additional detached residence of 90 m² or 186 m² by parcel size.

faq.q: Can a Hazelmere acreage add the usual Surrey SSMUH units?
faq.a: Generally not on the standard framing: the allowances apply to eligible lots under 4,050 m² inside the Urban Containment Boundary on community services. An acreage lot needs a parcel-level check of zone, containment boundary and servicing before any added-unit claim.

faq.q: Is a separate coach house allowed on an A-1 or ALR acreage here?
Which school is physically in Hazelmere?
faq.a: Catchments are still address-based and UNVERIFIED for any specific address — check the exact address in the SD36 locator before relying on a school.

faq.q: How many units are in Hazelmere Village?
faq.a: UNCONFIRMED. The strata plan obtained with the Form B package is where the unit count is properly confirmed.

The strata basis is strong — the complex is run by an elected strata council whose president signed a published testimonial for a strata-wide painting contract ( and listings record strata-style amenities including management.

faq.q: What pets are allowed at Hazelmere Village?
faq.a: A listing states "2 pets allowed, dogs to be no more than 44lbs" with no age restrictions ( — listing-stated only. Pet bylaws live in the strata's bylaws attached to the Form B; confirm there before counting on a specific dog.
